newsitem.title: CANADA: IMUTEC files for Mexico Virulizin approval.
newsitem.headline: IMUTEC files for Mexico Virulizin approval.

text.p: IMUTEC Corp said on Tuesday it applied for product registration of the cancer drug Virulizin with the Mexican Ministry of Health for the treatment of malignant melanoma.

IMUTEC said the application is based on the results of a Phase II clinical trial in 51 patients with advanced disease, completed in 1993 under the direction of the National Cancer Institute, which demonstrated that Virulizin provided patient benefit through improvements in survival and quality of life.

"Based on the positive results of the study, and with the support of the National Cancer Institute, we were encouraged (by the Ministry of Health) to file for marketing approval of Virulizin in Mexico as soon as possible," said IMUTEC president and chief executive Philippe Lacaille. "Because of the deadly nature of the disease, and the lack of effective therapy, we hope that the application will receive a speedy review."

IMUTEC said it has also taken the steps to explore the feasibility of filing for registration of Virulizin in other parts of the world where the problems associated with melanoma have become a serious national concern.
